objectives: This course examines the design of mechanisms to allocate scarce resources and the creation of marketplaces using economic theory. We will focus on two primary areas: auctions and matching. In the auctions module, we will study various settings, ranging from first-price sealed-bid auctions to search engine auctions. We will analyze the theoretical properties of each auction type and evaluate their predictions in real-world settings. In the matching module, we will study resource allocation without the use of prices, focusing on well-known algorithms and their desirable properties.
content:
1st and 2nd price sealed-bid auction
Dutch, English auction, revenue equivalence
eBay and combinatorial auctions
Keyword auctions and spectrum auctions
One-to-one matching, house allocation problem
Many-to-one matching, school choice problem
Kidney exchange problem
Liver exchange problem
Probabilistic assignments
books:
Haeringer, G. (2018). Market design: auctions and matching. MIT Press.
Milgrom, P. R. (2004). Putting auction theory to work. Cambridge University Press.
Roth, A. E., & Sotomayor, M. A. O. (1990). Two-Sided Matching: A Study in Game-Theoretic Modeling and Analysis. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
Che, Y. K., Chiappori, P. A., & Salanié, B. (2025). Handbook of the Economics of Matching (Vol. 2). Elsevier.
